name: Egg and Cheese Quesadilla
author: Ali Slagle
description: With its soft, gooey inside and toasted outside, this egg and cheese quesadilla is as satisfying to eat as it is fun to make. The trick is to use the barely set eggs and melted cheese to secure the fillings to the tortilla, so that when it’s time to flip, the whole quesadilla cleanly moves together. As the tortilla toasts, add another round of cheese and sprinkle some on the perimeter so it melts into a crisp, brown, lacy edge. If you’d like to add chopped vegetables like peppers, onions or kale, sauté them in the butter before adding the eggs.

ingredients.raw: ½ tablespoon unsalted or salted butter
Scant ½ cup grated Cheddar or Mexican cheese blend (scant 2 ounces)
ingredients.item: scant ½ cup grated cheddar or mexican cheese blend (scant 2 ounces)

steps.text: In a small bowl, beat the eggs and a pinch of salt with a fork until homogenous.

In a medium nonstick skillet — one that snugly fits your tortilla — melt the butter over medium heat. Add the eggs and swirl the pan so the eggs fill the skillet. Using a spatula, pull the eggs in toward the center and, while holding the spatula in place, tilt the pan so that the egg runs to the empty skillet. Repeat this until the surface is nearly set but still shiny, about 1 minute.

Sprinkle evenly with half of the cheese, then top with the tortilla and press to adhere. Put your hand in the middle of the tortilla. Flip the skillet so the tortilla is now on your hand, egg-side up. (Keep your arm away from the hot skillet, but otherwise nothing scary will happen because everything is adhered to the tortilla.) Place the tortilla, egg-side up, back in the skillet.

Sprinkle the remaining cheese on one half of the eggs, making sure to sprinkle some on the edge to crisp. Cook over medium until the tortilla is golden brown underneath, just a minute. Fold the tortilla in half, slide onto a plate, sprinkle with salt and cut into wedges.

name: Eggplant Involtini With Fresh Tomato Sauce
author: Hetty Lui McKinnon
description:
Think of this dish as an unbaked involtini, perfect for days when you are seeking minimal cooking-with-heat. This recipe allows each ingredient to shine: the smoky earthiness of grilled eggplant, the delicate creaminess of ricotta and the vibrant tang of ripe tomatoes. The only heat required is for pan-frying the thinly sliced globe eggplants (you could also grill them outside). Oiling the eggplant slices before they hit the pan prevents them from absorbing too much oil and becoming greasy. Stuffed with a zesty lemon-laced ricotta, the rolls bathe in a fresh, summery elixir of tomatoes, garlic and olive oil. A perfect light meal for a warm evening.

Watch Hetty Lui McKinnon make this dish in this video.

ingredients.raw: 1 ½ pounds (about 2 medium) globe eggplant, trimmed and cut lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick slices
ingredients.preparation: trimmed and cut lengthwise into ¼-inch-thick slices

ingredients.raw: 3 to 4 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 ½ cups (12 ounces) whole milk ricotta
Grated zest and juice of 1 lemon (about 3 tablespoons juice), plus ½ lemon for serving
ingredients.item: grated zest and juice of 1 lemon (about 3 tablespoons juice)

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil leaves, plus more whole leaves to serve
ingredients.preparation: plus more whole leaves to serve

ingredients.raw: 1 pound ripe tomatoes (such as beefsteak or Roma)
ingredients.item: ripe tomatoes (such as beefsteak or roma)

ingredients.raw: ½ to 1 teaspoon crushed red pepper (to your liking)

steps.text: Heat a large (12-inch) skillet on medium-high for 3 minutes.

While the pan is heating, place the eggplant slices on a cutting board, drizzle your hands with a little olive oil and spread the oil onto both sides of each slice to coat. Repeat with the remaining eggplant slices (you’ll need 2 to 3 tablespoons of oil in total).

Working in batches, lay as many slices of eggplant that will fit into your pan in a single layer, and season with a little salt and black pepper. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and then, using tongs or flexible spatula, flip over and repeat on the other side, cooking until golden and the eggplant is completely tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Continue cooking remaining eggplant. Set the cooked eggplant aside to cool.

Place the ricotta in a bowl and add the lemon zest, juice and basil. Season with ½ teaspoon of salt (taste and add more if needed, as different brands vary in flavor) and a big pinch of black pepper and stir to combine.

Using a box grater, grate the tomatoes and garlic (use the large holes for the tomatoes and finest holes for the garlic) directly into a shallow 10-inch serving dish. You’ll be left with some of the tomato skin, which you can chop up and add to the grated tomatoes or discard. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, the crushed red pepper, ½ teaspoon of salt and a generous pinch of black pepper. Stir well to combine.

Make the eggplant rolls: Place a heaped tablespoon of the ricotta filling onto the thicker end of an eggplant slice, roll it up and place it straight into the grated tomatoes (if the eggplant splits while rolling, that is fine, just keep going). Continue filling and rolling the remaining eggplant slices, placing them into the tomatoes as you go.
To serve, drizzle the eggplant rolls with olive oil, season with salt and pepper, squeeze over lemon juice and top with basil leaves. Serve immediately, as is, or with bread.
